Subject to the foregoing sentence, all Contractor employees and subcontractors who perform the Services will be referred to herein as “Representatives.” Contractor assumes full and sole responsibility for the acts of Representatives (including, without limitation, any breaches of Section 3), and for the payment of all compensation and expenses of these Representatives and for all state and federal income tax, unemployment insurance, social security, disability insurance, and other applicable withholdings. Further, Contractor will be responsible for acts or omissions of all of the Representatives to the same extent as if such acts or omissions were undertaken by Contractor, and for the purposes of this Agreement, work performed or acts or omissions undertaken by such Representatives will be deemed to have been performed or undertaken, as the case may be, by Contractor.

3.2 Obligations. Contractor will maintain in confidence the Confidential Information during the term of this Agreement and thereafter, will not disclose Confidential Information to any third parties other than Permitted Disclosees (as defined below) without Company’s prior written consent, and will not use such Confidential Information except as expressly permitted in this Agreement. Contractor will use the same degree of care in protecting the Confidential Information as Contractor uses to protect its own confidential and proprietary information from unauthorized use or disclosure, but in no event less than reasonable care. Contractor will use Confidential Information solely for the purpose of carrying out Contractor’s obligations under this Agreement. In addition, Contractor will not reproduce Confidential Information in any form except as required to accomplish Contractor’s obligations under this Agreement and will only disclose Confidential Information to its Affiliates, and its and its Affiliates’ directors, officers, employees and/or contractors who (a) have a need to know such Confidential Information in order for Contractor to perform its duties under this Agreement, and (b) are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than the non-disclosure obligations contained in this Section 3 prior to receiving any Confidential Information (“Permitted Disclosees”). Contractor will be responsible for breaches of this Section 3 by its Permitted Disclosees. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company may disclose this Agreement and any Confidential Information contained herein to actual or potential investors or purchasers, including such parties' legal and financial representatives, in connection with any Company financing, merger, or acquisition activities and the standard legal and financial due diligence conducted therewith; provided that, such investors or purchasers (and their legal and financial representatives) are bound by confidentiality obligations (which may include professional standards of conduct) no less restrictive than the non-disclosure obligations contained in this Section 3.

3.3 Exceptions. Confidential Information will not include information that: (a) is in or enters the public domain without breach of this Agreement through no fault of Contractor or third party wrongdoing; (b) Contractor can reasonably demonstrate was in its possession prior to first receiving it from Company; (c) Contractor can demonstrate was developed by Contractor independently, and without use of or reference to, the Confidential Information; or (d) Contractor receives from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of a nondisclosure obligation. In addition, Contractor may disclose Confidential Information that is required to be disclosed by law or by a subpoena or order issued by a court of competent jurisdiction

4.4 Third Party Technology. Contractor will specify in the applicable SOW all (a) Contractor IP, and (b) third party software, materials, work product or other third party technology (collectively, “Third-Party Technology”), included in or otherwise necessary for Company’s use of the Deliverables. Contractor will not use any such Contractor IP or Third Party Technology in any Deliverables unless Company agrees in writing (email acceptable) to such use. Company shall also have the right, but not the obligation, to review any associated licensing terms and conditions for such Third Party Technology prior to approving the same. If Company wishes to purchase Third Party Technology required in connection with its receipt of Services via Contractor as its reseller, such costs will be deemed Expenses (as defined below) under this Agreement. Contractor may issue Company a separate quotation for such Third Party Technology (provided that in the event any terms and conditions of such quotation conflict with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, this Agreement will govern). Unless Company has agreed in writing to enter into any associated licensing terms and conditions for approved Third Party Materials directly with the applicable vendor, Contractor must secure for Company’s benefit all necessary licenses, rights, clearances, and permissions to use the Third Party Materials for all purposes contemplated by this Agreement.

5.2.4 Third Party Technology. Contractor has (i) disclosed to Company, and obtained Company’s approval for, all Third Party Technology included in or otherwise necessary for Company’s use of the Deliverables, and (ii) not used any Third Party Technology that is subject to an Excluded License. “Excluded License” means any license (a) that would restrict the ability of Company to protect its proprietary interests in the Work Products or Company Materials, including protecting its Intellectual Property Rights therein, (b) requires the disclosure or distribution in source code form of any software subject to the Excluded License or any software used, based on, or distributed in connection with software subject to the Excluded License, (c) requires the licensing of any software subject to the Excluded License or any software used, based on, or distributed in connection with software subject to the Excluded License for the purpose of making derivative works, (d) imposes any restriction on the consideration to be charged for the distribution of any software subject to the Excluded License or any software used, based on, or distributed in connection with software subject to the Excluded License, or (e) creates, or purports to create, obligations for Company with respect to any Intellectual Property Rights or grants, or purports to grant, to any third party, any rights or immunities under any Company Intellectual Property Rights. Accordingly, Excluded Licenses include, but are not limited to, licenses incorporating copyleft requirements, such as, for example, any version of the GNU General Public License, GNU Lesser General Public License, SleepyCat License, or Mozilla Public License. For the avoidance of doubt, Company’s approval of a Third Party Technology and/or its licensing terms and conditions pursuant to Section 4.4 shall not relieve Contractor of any liability arising from a breach of this Section 5.2.4.

2.3. Subcontractors. Consultant may not subcontract or delegate any obligation under this Agreement without the prior written consent of Firma B. Consultant will cause any subcontractor that is so approved by Firma B (a “Permitted Subcontractor”), prior to such person’s performance of any Services, to execute a written agreement which, at a minimum, includes (a) an assignment of rights provision at least as broad as Section 5 (Intellectual Property Rights), and (b) a restrictions on the use and disclosure of Confidential Information (including Personal Information, if applicable) at least as stringent as those under Section 6 (Confidentiality). In any event, Consultant shall remain fully responsible for the acts or omissions of any Permitted Subcontractor that would be a breach of this Agreement if Consultant had taken such action or made such omission.

6.2. Obligations of Confidentiality. Consultant will hold in strict confidence and refrain from publication, dissemination, or any other disclosure to third parties of any Confidential Information, other than to Personnel and to Permitted Subcontractors who need to receive such Confidential Information to perform the Services in accordance with Section 2 (Personnel). Consultant will use Confidential Information only as required to perform the Services for Firma B. Consultant will not make copies of Confidential Information of Firma B, except as reasonably required to perform the Services or as specifically authorized to do so by Firma B.

6.3. Return of Confidential Information. Within fifteen (15) days following the expiration or termination of this Agreement, or at any time upon written request of the Firma B, Consultant will (a) return to Firma B all copies of Confidential Information, and (b) delete, erase and destroy all copies of Confidential Information located on Consultant’s computer drives and/or Consultant’s retained media, and will certify such deletion, erasure, and destruction of foregoing to Firma B.

8.2. Third Party Confidential Information and Materials. Consultant will not disclose to Firma B, or use, or induce Firma B to use, any confidential, proprietary or trade secret information of others. Performance of this Agreement will not breach any agreement or duty to keep in confidence or in trust confidential, proprietary or trade secret information of others that Consultant entered into prior to being retained by Firma B. Except as expressly set forth in the applicable Statement of Work, no third party software, technology or other materials will be incorporated in the Work Product. To the extent third party software, technology or other materials is identified in the Statement of Work as being incorporated in the Work Product, unless the Statement of Work expressly provides that Firma B need to obtain a license to use such software, technology or materials, Consultant will secure for Firma B sufficient rights to such software, technology or materials necessary for Firma B’s full use and enjoyment of the Work Product.

8.4 Publicity. Contractor will not, without the prior written consent of Company in each instance, use the name, service marks, or trademarks of Company or its Affiliates for any purpose, including any advertising, publicity release, or representative client list.

7.2 Effect of Termination. Upon any termination of this Agreement: (a) Contractor will promptly provide Company with all Confidential Information then in Contractor’s possession or destroy all copies of the Confidential Information, at Company’s sole discretion and direction, (b) Contractor will immediately provide Company with all Work Product, (c) Contractor, upon Company’s request, will reasonably assist Company in transitioning the Services, (d) Company will pay Contractor for any Services performed before the date of termination, and (e) each party’s obligations under this Agreement will immediately cease. Notwithstanding any terms to the contrary in this Agreement, Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.2, 8 and Exhibits B and C will survive any termination of this Agreement. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH HEREIN, IN NO EVENT WILL COMPANY BE LIABLE TO CONTRACTOR OR ANY THIRD PARTY FOR ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES OF ANY KIND ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING ANY TERMINATION OF THIS AGREEMENT PURSUANT TO SECTION 8.1.
